title: Open Clusters, Stellar Associations and Young Moving Groups: Dissolution, Mass Segregation and Kinematic Budgets Against Density and Energy Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Rekha Malhotra, and this is Open Clusters, Stellar Associations and Young Moving Groups: Dissolution, Mass Segregation and Kinematic Budgets Against Density and Energy Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Rekha Malhotra, and this is Open Clusters, Stellar Associations and Young Moving Groups: Dissolution, Mass Segregation and Kinematic Budgets Against Density and Energy Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Binding Energy Budget of Westerlund 2: The Gravitational Account of a Very Massive Young Cluster'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): mean_stellar_mass_Msun = 4; crossing_time_Myr = 0.215114; half_mass_relaxation_time_Myr = 13.3004; half_mass_density_Msun_pc3 = 1793.63; half_mass_number_density_pc3 = 448.408; virial_dispersion_km_s = 3.61013; virial_parameter_alpha = 1.5985; escape_speed_at_Rh_km_s = 12.5059; kinetic_energy_J = 1.49135e+42; binding_energy_abs_J = 1.24396e+42; energy_ratio_T_over_

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Binding Energy Budget of Westerlund 2: The Gravitational Account of a Very Massive Young Cluster”. Its stated result is: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): mean_stellar_mass_Msun = 4; crossing_time_Myr = 0.215114; half_mass_relaxation_time_Myr = 13.3004; half_mass_density_Msun_pc3 = 1793.63; half_mass_number_density_pc3 = 448.408; virial_dispersion_km_s = 3.61013; virial_parameter_alpha = 1.5985; esc (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Binding Energy Budget of Westerlund 2: The Gravitational Account of a Very Massive Young Cluster'; 'Cluster and Ring Budget of the Lambda Orionis Region: A Small Bound Core Inside an Expanding Shell'; 'Coherence Budget of the AB Doradus Moving Group at an Age Beyond One Hundred Million Years'; 'Density and Binding Budget of Trumpler 14: A Massive Young Cluster at the Opposite Extreme from an Association'; 'Density and Crossing Budget of IC 2602: A Young Southern Cluster Counted in Its Own Crossing Times'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.
